title: SemVer policy and upgrade gates for serving runtime
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Define an operational semver policy and a prescriptive rollout + upgrade-gating model for the Redwood serving runtime. This ticket captures the definition of what constitutes breaking changes vs compatible changes, deprecation windows, LTS channel behavior, automated canary/fallback gates, and the upgrade tooling changes required so customers and Dedicated/Private deployments can upgrade predictably.
background: We currently lack a single authoritative spec for runtime compatibility and LTS behavior. Past rollouts have caused confusion about what triggers a major version, how long older minor lines are supported, and how automatic rollouts should be gated. This leads to conservative rollouts, manual intervention, and customer upgrade friction. The goal is to standardize expectations and implement tooling to enforce gates.
policy_summary: Adopt strict Semantic Versioning for the runtime binaries and API surface: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. MAJOR increments may contain breaking changes and require explicit customer opt-in or migration tooling. MINOR releases may add functionality and non-breaking API surface changes; PATCH releases are bugfixes and security patches only. Public RPCs/REST endpoints and on-disk state formats are compatibility boundaries; anything that changes them is treated as a breaking change unless a documented compatibility shim exists.
breaking_changes_definition: Breaking change = any change that causes one or more of the following without automatic compatibility: (1) Existing client requests to error or change semantics; (2) Incompatible on-disk cache/KV layout change requiring migration; (3) Removal of a documented API field or status code; (4) Behavioral changes that violate documented SLOs (latency/throughput) in a way that cannot be mitigated via configuration. All breaking changes must be gated behind MAJOR version bumps or explicit opt-in flags and require a migration guide.
deprecation_policy: When a field/endpoint/behavior is deprecated: (1) Announce deprecation in release notes and console changelog at least one MINOR cycle before removal (target 90 days minimum); (2) Mark as deprecated in SDKs and server logs with telemetry event 'runtime.deprecation.warning'; (3) Provide migration steps and automated converters where feasible; (4) Removal only allowed in next MAJOR or by explicit opt-in flag in a MINOR release when customers have been notified.
lts_strategy: Introduce two simultaneous channels: 'stable' (rolling minors, default) and 'lts' (long-term support). LTS lines are selected from a MINOR that meets stability criteria (no regressions for 8 weeks; adoption > 20% of internal e2e clusters). LTS receive critical patches (PATCH and high-severity MINOR backports) for 12 months. Major upgrades from LTS to next major are opt-in and require migration testing. LTS selection is announced with a separate 'lts' tag and release notes.
rollout_gates: All runtime releases must pass a standard gate sequence before wide rollout: (1) CI unit & integration; (2) Canary (1% internal traffic) for 48 hours with performance baselines; (3) Progressive canary ramp to 10% over 72 hours with real workload telemetry; (4) Staged customer cohorts (beta customers, then all). Gate checks: error rate, 95th latency, memory/kv-miss ratios, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost per token. A defined rollback window is 6 hours after each ramp step unless manual approval extends it.
rollback_criteria: Automatic rollback triggers: error rate delta > 2x baseline sustained for 10 minutes; 95p latency regression > 30% over baseline; KV cache hit rate drop > 15% causing increased token compute. Manual rollback possible for any other high-severity customer impact. Rollback must be executed via the release controller and documented in the rollback incident note with linked PR and telemetry snapshots.
upgrade_tooling_changes: Add new 'redwoodctl runtime upgrade' command with flags: --channel (stable|lts|canary), --dry-run, --force, --rollback-on-failure. The controller will compute safe upgrade windows using per-tenant SLOs and will provide preflight checks (disk layout compatibility, plugin ABI checks, model artifact schema checks). The tooling will emit structured upgrade events (upgrade.start, upgrade.step, upgrade.complete, upgrade.rollback) to the observability pipeline.
compatibility_matrix_summary: Documented matrix will include: runtime binary version, on-disk cache format version, API schema version, SDK compatibility ranges, and supported GPU kernel versions. Rule: clients built against runtime X.Y.Z are guaranteed to work with runtime X.(Y+N).Z for N >= 0 (backward compatibility for MINOR bumps), but not guaranteed across MAJOR increases. Matrix maintained in repo under docs/compatibility and surfaced in Console.
migration_steps: For any change classified as breaking, provide: (1) migration guide in docs with code snippets; (2) test plan for Dedicated and Private customers; (3) a migration script or converter if state change is required; (4) a version-skew policy that guarantees up to one MINOR of skew during rolling upgrades. Include a checklist for release engineers.
testing_requirements: Mandatory tests before canary: full integration tests with KV cache enabled, perf regression benchmark against representative prompt mix, end-to-end scenarios for model serving correctness, and cross-version backward compatibility smoke tests. A dedicated 'upgrade-sanity' test pool must run on any candidate build against the latest LTS image.
monitoring_and_alerting: Instrument these metrics for gating: runtime.errors, runtime.latency_p95, runtime.kv_hit_rate, runtime.mem_rss, runtime.gpu_util, upgrade.events. Create alert burn-rate rules tied to canary weights and a dashboard template for release owners. Telemetry must include release metadata and canary cohort tags.
communication_plan: Publish release notes and deprecation timelines to Console, changelog, and #releases slack channel. Notify Dedicated/Private customers via account managers and schedule migration windows. Provide per-release 'What changed / Action required' summary in Console and an FAQ link. For LTS candidates, issue an advance notice 30 days prior to selection.
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Agreed on strict semver with MAJOR for breaking changes (decision by Release WG).
2026-03-03: Chose 12 month LTS support window; pragmatic backport policy for critical MINOR fixes.
2026-03-09: Mandated automated rollback triggers and core set of telemetry metrics for gating.
next_steps: Finalize semver language and publish to docs/compatibility/semver.md
Implement 'redwoodctl runtime upgrade' prototype and wire upgrade.events into observability
Add compatibility matrix page to Console and link to SDKs
Run tabletop drill for rollback and document incident playbook
acceptance_criteria: Semver doc merged into main repo; release-controller accepts channel flags; at least one canary rollout executed with the new gating checks in staging; compatibility matrix scaffolded in Console. All changes reviewed by Release WG and Security.
notes: Keep the policy intentionally conservative in language — aim to reduce customer surprise while enabling fast iteration. This ticket focuses on the policy and infra hooks; follow-ups will operationalize advanced migration tooling and SDK deprecation helpers.
